lines.en: Chloe, I have a terrible story. When I reached my door, I realised I had left my keys inside.
lines.pt: Chloe, tenho uma história terrível. Quando cheguei à porta, percebi que tinha deixado as chaves lá dentro.

lines.en: Oh dear! Where had you put them? Do you remember leaving them on the kitchen table?
lines.pt: Ai, ai! Onde você as tinha colocado? Lembra de tê-las deixado na mesa da cozinha?

lines.en: Yes, I found out that I had put them next to my phone charger.
lines.pt: Sim, descobri que eu as tinha colocado ao lado do carregador do celular.

lines.en: So you were locked out! Had you called anyone before you came to find me?
lines.pt: Então você ficou trancada para fora! Você tinha ligado para alguém antes de vir me procurar?

lines.en: I had tried your number, but I realised I had saved it wrongly last year.
lines.pt: Eu tinha tentado o seu número, mas percebi que o tinha salvo errado no ano passado.

lines.en: What a nightmare! I discovered I had made the same mistake with my brother’s number last month.
lines.pt: Que pesadelo! Descobri que eu tinha cometido o mesmo erro com o número do meu irmão no mês passado.

lines.en: Anyway, I had a spare key at my neighbour’s house, but I had forgotten that too.
lines.pt: Enfim, eu tinha uma chave reserva na casa da minha vizinha, mas tinha me esquecido disso também.

lines.en: Then how did you get in? Had the neighbour come home by the time you rang?
lines.pt: Então como você entrou? A vizinha já tinha chegado em casa quando você tocou?

lines.en: Yes, she had just arrived with her shopping, and she remembered where the key was.
lines.pt: Sim, ela tinha acabado de chegar com as compras e lembrou onde estava a chave.

lines.en: Lucky you! Last winter I found out that I had lost mine, and a locksmith charged a lot.
lines.pt: Que sorte! No inverno passado descobri que tinha perdido a minha, e um chaveiro cobrou muito.

lines.en: I believe it. From now on, I will check my pockets before I close the door.
lines.pt: Acredito. De agora em diante, vou conferir os bolsos antes de fechar a porta.

facts.label: Past perfect depois de realised
facts.sub: Percebi que tinha: realised I had + particípio. Descobri que tinha: found out that I had + particípio. Pergunta: Where had you…?

facts.label: Percebeu
facts.sub: Realised that + had + particípio mostra algo que você percebe depois. A percepção fica no passado simples: I realised I had left my keys. Em português, “percebi que tinha deixado”. O that pode ser omitido.

facts.label: Descobriu
facts.sub: Found out é phrasal verb: find out, found out. Use com had: I found out that I had put them there. Em português, “descobri que tinha colocado”. Discovered é mais formal e também aceita had + particípio.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: In “I realised I had forgotten”, the forgetting came first.
We say “I realised I have forgotten” in past stories.
“She found out he had left” means he left first.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: In “I realised I had forgotten”, the forgetting came first. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I realised I have forgotten” in past stories. → Falso (We say I had forgotten.)
“She found out he had left” means he left first. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A story from a windy street · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a windy afternoon on a steep street in Edinburgh. Old grey buildings stand above the busy pavement. Dora walks quickly, with a red face and cold hands. Her friend Sara is waiting outside a small bookshop. Something has gone wrong this afternoon. Dora needs to explain what she realised too late.

“Sara, I have a terrible story. When I reached my door, I realised I had left my keys inside.” says Dora. “Oh dear! Where had you put them? Do you remember leaving them on the kitchen table?” says Sara. “Yes, I found out that I had put them next to my phone charger.” says Dora.
